Presentation: Stack root screen, no header, full-screen; left via router.replace (no back)
Entry points: App cold launch. The native splash is held (SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync) until the 5 Poppins weights have loaded, then this animated JS splash takes over. Shown on every launch, even when a saved session token exists.
Exits: Automatic only, no buttons: when the exit animation finishes → router.replace('/onboarding') (Onboarding – Sign-in).
Purpose: Branded animated launch screen showing the compass mark, the Jourrrney wordmark and the tagline before sign-in.
Layout (top to bottom): Full-bleed diagonal gradient (#0d1117 → #0D5C63 at 45% → #1a0a02, start 0.1,0 → end 0.9,1) → vertically and horizontally centred group: CompassMark 80px (cream disc, dark-green ring, 8 ticks, 'N', two-tone needle) → 24px gap → wordmark 'Jourrrney' → tagline 'ROUTE · ROAM · REPEAT'
Key copy (verbatim): Jourrrney | ROUTE · ROAM · REPEAT
Interactions: None (non-interactive). Timeline: 200 ms delay → 500 ms ease-out fade-in + scale 0.96→1 → hold until 2600 ms → 600 ms fade-out + scale 1→1.05 → hand-off to /onboarding. The compass needle loops a gentle wobble (+6°, −5°, 0°; 1.4 s / 1.8 s / 1.2 s sine ease). Total on screen about 3.2 s.
States: Single visual state. No loading, error, empty or signed-in/out variants. Not theme-aware (always the dark gradient regardless of light/dark setting). The pre-font native splash is a separate, earlier layer (app.json has no splash entry, so it is Expo's default).
Data & state: No data. app/_layout.tsx: useFonts(Poppins 400/500/600/700/800) gates rendering; bootstrapProfileSession() restores a saved token in the background but does NOT gate or change this screen; useAutoUpdate() applies published OTA updates. Note: URL '/' is shared by this route and (tabs)/index; navigation uses the explicit '/(tabs)' group path.
Design notes / findings: Poppins SemiBold for wordmark (34) and tagline (11, letter-spacing 4, white 50%). Teal #0D5C63 is the mid gradient stop. Compass colours: disc #F5F0E8, ring/ticks/north needle #2C4A3E, south needle #C45A2A. Root StatusBar uses dark icons in light mode, which sit over this dark gradient. Source of truth: Figma '0.0 Splash Screen' (layout) + Make prototype (timing).
Suggested Figma frame name: S001 · Splash

Presentation: Stack screen, no header; entered via router.replace (no back to Splash)
Entry points: Splash auto hand-off (router.replace). Shown after the splash on every cold start.
Exits: Skip, any of the three social buttons, or a successfully verified 6-digit code → router.replace('/(tabs)') (Home – Discover). It no longer hands off to /location-permission.
Purpose: Optional two-step sign-in wrapper that swaps between the Email step and the Confirm-code step on one dark gradient background.
Layout (top to bottom): Full-screen vertical gradient (#0b1520 → #0D2B2E at 40% → #1C1917, top to bottom) → currently active step (Step 1 Email, or Step 2 Confirm code) filling the screen; safe-area top inset is passed to both steps, bottom inset to Step 1 only
Key copy (verbatim): (copy lives in the two step rows)
Interactions: Step swap is instant, no transition animation in code: Email → Confirm after requestCode succeeds; Confirm → Email via the back arrow (email text is kept).
States: step = email | confirm; sending / verifying booleans; sendError / verifyError strings; devCode string (dev hint echoed by backend). Always dark: ignores the light/dark theme setting.
Data & state: useProfileStore: signIn(provider) (Google/Facebook/Apple are LOCAL-ONLY fake sign-in that just flags the user as signed in), skip() (clears any session), requestCode(email) and verifyCode(email, code) → journey-backend (code generated and checked server-side; no email actually sent yet; backend echoes devCode outside production).
Design notes / findings: Sign-in is deliberately non-mandatory; every button leads into the app. No Figma frame existed; built from user-supplied reference screenshots adapted to the dark gradient + compass mark. Social providers need developer-console credentials that do not exist yet, so they are placeholders.
Suggested Figma frame name: S002 · Onboarding – Sign-in (container)

Screen / frame name: Onboarding – Step 1: Sign in or create an account
Presentation: Inline step (full screen)
Entry points: First thing shown on /onboarding; also reached by tapping the back arrow on Step 2.
Exits: Skip (X + 'Skip', top-left) → skip() then router.replace('/(tabs)'). Google / Facebook / Apple buttons → local signIn(provider) then router.replace('/(tabs)'). Continue → requestCode(); on success → Step 2; on failure stays here with an inline error. Terms of Service / Privacy Policy text is styled like links but is NOT tappable.
Purpose: Collect an email (or pick a social provider, or skip) to unlock personalised planning, saved itineraries and safety tools.
Layout (top to bottom): Top row (safe-area top + 12): [X icon 22 white + 'Skip' label] left, CompassMark 32px right → title (2 lines) → subtitle → email input (52px high, fully rounded pill, 1px white-25% border) → [inline red error, only on failure] → 'Continue' button (full-width pill, 16px vertical padding) → divider row (hairline – 'or' – hairline) → 3 stacked outlined pill buttons (Google / Facebook / Apple, 12px gap, brand icon + label) → legal line (Terms of Service / Privacy Policy) → centred footer wordmark 'JOURRRNEY'
Key copy (verbatim): Skip | Sign in or create (line break) an account | Unlock personalised trip planning, saved itineraries, and safety tools across Jourrrney. | Email | Continue | Sending code… | or | Sign in with Google | Sign in with Facebook | Sign in with Apple | By continuing, you agree to Jourrrney's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. | JOURRRNEY | Couldn't send a code — try again. (fallback error)
Interactions: Type email (email-address keyboard, no auto-capitalise); tap Continue (disabled until the field has non-whitespace text); tap a social button (instant local sign-in, no OAuth sheet); tap Skip. No scrolling and no KeyboardAvoidingView in this step, so the keyboard overlays the lower part of the layout.
States: Default: Continue disabled (white 15% fill, white 50% label). Email typed: Continue enabled (cream #FBF7F2 fill, indigo #333C81 label). Sending: spinner + 'Sending code…', input not editable, button disabled. Error: red message below the input (backend message or fallback). Always dark theme. Social buttons have no pressed/disabled/loading visuals.
Data & state: Props from OnboardingLogin: email, loading, error, topInset, bottomInset. SOCIAL_BUTTONS constant (google/facebook/apple). requestCode() → journey-backend; signIn()/skip() on useProfileStore.
Design notes / findings: Poppins Bold 28/34 title, Regular 13/19 subtitle (white 60%), Bold 15 button label, Bold 14 social labels. Pill radius 999 on input and buttons. Cream #FBF7F2 primary button on dark gradient with indigo #333C81 text. Link colour #8B93D6 for Terms/Privacy. Apple icon rendered white; Google/Facebook use their own brand colours. Footer wordmark Poppins SemiBold 11, letter-spacing 2, white 35%, bottom padding max(inset, 20).
Suggested Figma frame name: S003 · Onboarding – Step 1: Sign in or create an account

Screen / frame name: Onboarding – Step 1 states: sending code & error
Parent screen: Onboarding – Step 1: Sign in or create an account
Presentation: Inline state
Entry points: Tap Continue with an email entered (sending); backend unreachable or rejects the email (error).
Exits: Success → Step 2 (Confirm code). Failure → stays on Step 1; user can edit and retry or use social/Skip.
Purpose: Show the request-in-flight and failure feedback for the email code request.
Layout (top to bottom): Same as Step 1, with: input dimmed/non-editable → (error only) red message text under the input, input bottom margin shrinks from 16 to 8 → Continue button shows a small indigo spinner left of the label
Key copy (verbatim): Sending code… | Couldn't send a code — try again. (fallback; the backend's own error string is shown when provided)
Interactions: While sending: input and Continue are disabled; social buttons and Skip remain tappable. After failure: editing the email and tapping Continue retries (error clears when a new request starts).
States: loading=true → label 'Sending code…' + ActivityIndicator, button grey; error string present → red #F87171 12px/17 message. No empty-email error: Continue is simply disabled.
Data & state: sending / sendError state in OnboardingLogin; result of useProfileStore.requestCode(email.trim()).
Design notes / findings: Error text colour #F87171 (the dark-theme danger red), Poppins Regular 12. Spinner colour #333C81 on the cream button, but the button turns translucent grey while loading, so the indigo spinner sits on a grey fill.
Suggested Figma frame name: S004 · Onboarding – Step 1 states: sending code & error

Screen / frame name: Onboarding – Step 2: Let's confirm your email
Presentation: Inline step (full screen)
Entry points: Continue on Step 1 after the backend accepted the email.
Exits: Back arrow (top-left) → Step 1 (email kept). Continue with 6 digits → verifyCode(); success → router.replace('/(tabs)'); failure stays with inline error. 'Resend code' → requests a new code and restarts the cooldown. 'Enter password instead' → native alert saying it is not available.
Purpose: Let the user type the 6-digit code that was 'sent' to their email to finish sign-in.
Layout (top to bottom): Back arrow (ArrowLeft 22, #8B93D6, top-left at safe-area top + 12) → title → explanatory paragraph with the email in semi-bold → [dev-only gold hint with the actual code] → code input (52px, radius 16, centred-ish large letter-spaced digits) → [inline red error] → 'Continue' cream pill button → centred 'Didn't receive a code?' + either a countdown line or a 'Resend code' link → 'Enter password instead' link
Key copy (verbatim): Let's confirm your email | Enter the secure code we sent to {email}. Check junk mail if it's not in your inbox. | Dev mode — no email is sent yet, your code is {devCode} | 6-digit code | Continue | Confirming… | Didn't receive a code? | You can request another code in {n}s | Resend code | Enter password instead | That code didn't work — try again. (fallback error)
Interactions: Type digits (numeric keypad; non-digits stripped, max 6); Continue enabled only at exactly 6 digits; tap back arrow; tap Resend (only after the 30 s cooldown); tap 'Enter password instead'. No auto-submit on the 6th digit, no per-digit OTP boxes (single text field).
States: Default: Continue disabled. 6 digits entered: Continue enabled. Verifying: spinner + 'Confirming…', input not editable. Error: red message under input (wrong code, expired, too many attempts, or backend unreachable). Resend cooldown: countdown text for 30 s, then link; resending shows a small #8B93D6 spinner in place of the link. Dev hint only appears when the backend returns devCode (non-production). Always dark theme.
Data & state: Props: email, loading, error, devCode, topInset, onBack/onConfirm/onResend. Local state: code, cooldown (starts at 30 s on mount, counts down each second), resending. verifyCode(email, code) and requestCode(email) on useProfileStore → journey-backend.
Design notes / findings: Poppins Bold 26 title; body 13/19 white 60% (email in SemiBold white 85%); code field Poppins SemiBold 16, letter-spacing 4, radius 16 (note: the Step 1 email field is a full pill, this one is not); links #8B93D6 Bold 13; dev hint gold #C9981F SemiBold 12. This step has no Skip button, no compass mark and no footer wordmark, unlike Step 1. 'Enter password instead' is an honest placeholder (no password auth exists).
Suggested Figma frame name: S005 · Onboarding – Step 2: Let's confirm your email

Screen / frame name: Onboarding – Step 2 states: verifying, error & resend cooldown
Parent screen: Onboarding – Step 2: Let's confirm your email
Presentation: Inline state
Entry points: Tap Continue with 6 digits (verifying); failed verification (error); 30 s after arriving or after a resend (resend link available).
Exits: Success → router.replace('/(tabs)'). Failure → stays; edit code and retry.
Purpose: Show verification progress, failure feedback and the resend-code timer.
Layout (top to bottom): Same as Step 2, with: input not editable while verifying → red error line under the input (input bottom margin 16 → 8) → Continue button with indigo spinner + 'Confirming…' → helper block switches between 'You can request another code in {n}s' (muted, 30→0) and the tappable 'Resend code' link (or a spinner while resending)
Key copy (verbatim): Confirming… | That code didn't work — try again. | You can request another code in {n}s | Resend code | Didn't receive a code?
Interactions: Resend is only tappable once the countdown reaches 0; a successful resend restarts the 30 s countdown and refreshes the dev hint code. A failed resend silently does nothing visible (no error message).
States: verifying | error | cooldown>0 | cooldown=0 (Resend code link) | resending (spinner). Dev-mode hint line appears between the paragraph and the input when devCode exists.
Data & state: verifying / verifyError in OnboardingLogin; cooldown / resending local to ConfirmCodeStep; handleResend → requestCode then setDevCode.
Design notes / findings: Muted helper text Poppins Regular 13, white 55%, centred. Error colour #F87171. Spinner #8B93D6 for resend, #333C81 for Continue.
Suggested Figma frame name: S006 · Onboarding – Step 2 states: verifying, error & resend cooldown

Parent screen: Onboarding – Step 2: Let's confirm your email
Presentation: Native system alert (Alert.alert), centred dialog
Entry points: Tap 'Enter password instead' on Step 2.
Exits: OK (system default button) → dismisses and returns to Step 2.
Purpose: Honestly tell the user password sign-in does not exist yet instead of silently continuing.
Layout (top to bottom): Native alert: title → message → single default OK button
Key copy (verbatim): Password sign-in | Not available yet — this app only supports email-code sign-in right now.
Interactions: Tap OK to dismiss.
States: Single state. Appearance is the iOS/Android system alert and follows the OS appearance, not the app's palette.
Data & state: None (static Alert.alert call).
Design notes / findings: Not a custom component, so a designer only needs a native-alert reference; consider whether to replace with a custom sheet or remove the link until password auth exists.
Suggested Figma frame name: S007 · Onboarding – Password sign-in unavailable alert

Exits: 'Allow While Using App' → shows the OS foreground-location permission dialog, then (allowed or denied) router.replace('/(tabs)'). 'Not Now' → router.replace('/(tabs)').
Purpose: Pre-permission explainer asking to use the user's location for live distances and travel times.
Layout (top to bottom): Top padding = safe-area top + 40 → 100×100 rounded-24 square tinted with the primary colour at 12% → (20px below, separate element, not inside the square) MapPin icon 40 in primary → title → explanatory paragraph → 'Allow While Using App' filled button → 'Not Now' text button → centred footnote

Primary button fixed indigo #333C81, radius 16, white Poppins Bold 14; 'Not Now' uses textSecondary. Background c.bg (#FBF7F2 light / #15120E dark). Bottom padding max(inset, 24). Source: Figma '1.1.1 Location Permission Prompt'.
Suggested Figma frame name: S008 · Location permission prompt

Presentation: Tab (first bottom tab, 'Discover'), no header
Entry points: After onboarding (Skip / social / verified code → router.replace('/(tabs)'), or after location-permission); Discover tab in the bottom bar; Back from pushed screens.
Exits: Hero greeting block / suggestion row / unambiguous search submit → /destination/[id]; ambiguous or non-India search submit → /search/results?q=…; hero shield button and 'Her Journey' quick action and Safest 'See all' → /(tabs)/safety; 'Plan Trip' quick action → /(tabs)/plan; 'Explore All' and Popular 'See all' → /search/results; any card → /destination/[id]; Recently Viewed 'See all' → /recently-viewed; recent-search card → /destination/[id] or /search/results?q=…; profile pill → /profile (modal).
Purpose: Main discovery feed: inspiration hero with search, category filter, shortcuts to planning and safety, and curated destination rails.
Layout (top to bottom): Hero carousel 380px tall, full-bleed under the status bar (photo, scrim, logo + safety button header, dots, greeting + location caption, search pill) → category chips (24px above and below) → 3 quick-action tiles → 'Popular Destinations' rail (≤8 grid cards) → 'Safest for Women & Solo Travel' rail (5 grid cards with safety score) → [if any] 'Recently Viewed' rail → [if any] 'Recent Searches' rail of small cards → bottom spacer (tab bar height + 24). Floating bottom tab bar and profile pill sit above the scroll.
Key copy (verbatim): Where do you want to go? | Where will you Jourrrney next? | Good Morning 👋 / Good Afternoon 👋 / Good Evening 👋 | All | Heritage | Beach | Nature | Adventure | Plan Trip | Her Journey | Explore All | Popular Destinations | See all | Safest for Women & Solo Travel | Recently Viewed | Recent Searches | No matches yet — keep typing, or hit search to browse all destinations.
Interactions: Vertical scroll (keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled' so suggestion taps work); each rail and the chip row scroll horizontally; tap chips to filter Popular rail; tap tiles, cards, See all links; type in the hero search bar for live suggestions; hero auto-advances every 4 s.
States: Category: All (default) / Heritage / Beach / Nature / Adventure. Fresh install: Recently Viewed and Recent Searches sections are completely absent (no empty placeholder). Suggestions dropdown open/closed. Light and dark both supported for everything below the hero (hero itself is always dark-scrim over photo). No loading or error state (all data is local).
Data & state: DESTINATIONS (static data/destinations.ts; items with hidden=true are excluded from Popular, Safest and Search browse); womenSafety.score sorts the Safest rail; useRecentSearchesStore (searches, max 10, in-memory); useRecentlyViewedStore (destinationIds, max 5, written by Destination detail on mount, in-memory); useThemeColors(); tabBarHeight from useBottomTabBarHeight().
Design notes / findings: Poppins Bold 16 section titles with accent-coloured 'See all >' (green c.success for the Safest rail, indigo otherwise); horizontal rails use 16px side padding and 12px gaps; page rhythm is 24px between sections. Quick-action tiles tint their theme accent (indigo / teal / gold) at 10% fill with 20% 1.5px border, emoji 24, label Poppins ExtraBold 11. Background c.bg. Source: Figma '1.1 Home Feed'.

Screen / frame name: Home – Hero carousel with greeting & search
Presentation: Inline (top block of the Home scroll, 380px)
Entry points: Top of Home – Discover.
Exits: Greeting/location block → /destination/[id] for the slide showing; shield button → /(tabs)/safety; search submit → /destination/[id] (unambiguous) or /search/results?q=…; suggestion row → /destination/[id].
Purpose: Inspirational photo hero that rotates through three real destinations and hosts the app's only Home search bar.
Layout (top to bottom): Destination photo (heroImage, cover, cross-fades between slides) → vertical dark scrim gradient (rgba(0,0,0,0.55) → rgba(0,0,0,0.2) at 40% → rgba(28,25,23,0.92)) → header row at safe-area top + 8 (CompassMark 28 + 'Jourrrney' left; 36px translucent-white circle with Shield icon right, offset 70px from the edge to clear the profile pill) → dot indicators at y=100 (3 dots, active one is an 18×6 white pill, others 6px at 40% opacity) → greeting block 90px above the bottom on a light-tint frosted BlurView panel (intensity 16, radius 20): small greeting line, two-line headline with 'Jourrrney' in indigo, location caption row → search pill 20px from the bottom
Key copy (verbatim): Jourrrney | Good Morning 👋 / Good Afternoon 👋 / Good Evening 👋 | Where will you (line break) Jourrrney next? | {name}, {state} | — tap to explore → | Where do you want to go?
Interactions: Auto-advance every 4 s with a 300 ms fade-out / fade-in (no swipe, dots not tappable). Tap the greeting block to open the current destination. Search field: type for live suggestions, return key labelled 'search' submits.
States: Slides: Agra → Ladakh → Jaipur (HERO_IDS; destination name and state in the caption change with the slide). Greeting by hour: before 12:00 Good Morning, before 17:00 Good Afternoon, otherwise Good Evening. Search field empty / focused / typed (suggestions dropdown row). Renders nothing if none of the three hero ids exist.
Data & state: HERO_DESTINATIONS from DESTINATIONS ids agra, ladakh, jaipur; local state index, query, inputFocused; useRecentSearchesStore.addSearch; matchDestination helpers (findLiveMatches, resolveUnambiguousMatch, matchNonIndiaPlace); safe-area insets.

Greeting Poppins Regular 13 white 60%; headline Poppins SemiBold 30/36 white with 'Jourrrney' in #333C81, which is dark indigo on a dark photo (low contrast); caption MapPin #333C81 14 + Regular 12 white 55%, arrow part white 30%. Search pill: 52px high, radius 18, white 96%, shadow (opacity 0.18, radius 20), Search icon #333C81, placeholder #78716C. USE_GREETING_BACKDROP_BLUR flag = true (experiment; false would use glow only). Header and hero stay dark in both app themes.
Suggested Figma frame name: S010 · Home – Hero carousel with greeting & search

Presentation: Inline floating panel anchored under the hero search pill (hero zIndex raised to 20 while open)
Entry points: Focus the hero search field and type at least one non-space character.
Exits: Tap a suggestion → records the search and opens /destination/[id]; keyboard search key → /destination/[id] (single unambiguous match) or /search/results?q=…
Purpose: Live autocomplete of destination names (typo-tolerant) as the user types.
Layout (top to bottom): Panel (16px side margins, top 368, max height 280, radius 16, surface colour, drop shadow) → up to 5 rows, each: 40×40 radius-10 destination photo → name (1 line) over state (1 line) → small Search icon at the right; 1px soft divider between rows → OR a single padded empty message
Key copy (verbatim): No matches yet — keep typing, or hit search to browse all destinations.
Interactions: Tap row (works while keyboard is up; blur is delayed 150 ms to let the tap register). Typing updates results on every keystroke; ranking = prefix, then fuzzy, with recent searches and review count as tie-breakers.
States: Hidden when the field is unfocused or empty. Results (1–5 rows). Empty (no match) message. Known non-India place (e.g. Dubai) → no suggestions, so it shows the same empty message (Home has no dedicated India-only message; Search results does). Theme-aware (surface / text colours).
Data & state: findLiveMatches(query, 5, recentIds) ranked with useRecentSearchesStore ids; matchNonIndiaPlace(query) suppresses matching; addSearch(query, d.id) on select.
Design notes / findings: Name Poppins SemiBold 13, state Regular 11 textSecondary, icon c.textMuted 13. Shadow 0.2 / radius 16 / offset y6 (elevation 8). The panel overflows the 380px hero box and overlaps the category chips / Popular Destinations below.
Suggested Figma frame name: S011 · Home – Hero search suggestions dropdown

Presentation: Inline filter chips + filtered rail
Entry points: Tap any chip in the horizontal chip row under the hero.
Exits: None by itself; 'See all' on the filtered rail still goes to /search/results (the chosen category is not passed along).
Purpose: Filter the first rail of Home by destination category.
Layout (top to bottom): Horizontal chip row (16px side padding, 8px gap): 36px-high pills 'All' | 'Heritage' | 'Beach' | 'Nature' | 'Adventure' → below, the rail's title swaps from 'Popular Destinations' to the category name, rail shows up to 8 matching grid cards
Key copy (verbatim): All | Heritage | Beach | Nature | Adventure | Popular Destinations (when All) | {category name} (otherwise) | See all
Interactions: Tap to select one chip (single select, no deselect other than choosing All); selection is local and resets when the screen remounts.

Data & state: activeCategory local state; featured = DESTINATIONS where !hidden and category.includes(activeCategory).

Exits: 'See all' → /recently-viewed; any card → /destination/[id].
Purpose: Quick return to the last destinations the user opened.
Layout (top to bottom): Section header row ('Recently Viewed' left, indigo 'See all >' right) → horizontal rail of up to 5 grid DestinationCards (rating stat), most recent first
Key copy (verbatim): Recently Viewed | See all
Interactions: Horizontal scroll; tap card; tap See all.

Exits: Card with a resolved destination → /destination/[id]; card whose query matched no single destination → /search/results?q={query}.

Exits: Tap a destination row → /destination/[id]; Back gesture → previous screen.
Purpose: Browse the full list of destinations with a category filter, and search by name.

Interactions: Tap the field (switches to Suggestion mode); tap chips to filter; scroll the list; tap a row. The indigo filter button has no handler (visual placeholder).

Zero results shows '0 destinations found' with a blank list and no empty illustration. Opening with a q param starts directly in Suggestion mode. Light/dark supported.
